title: Regularity ascends along flat maps with regular fibres
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, S an R-algebra. Suppose R is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], S is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], the map R → S is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and for every prime p of R the fibre p.Fiber S [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular ring. Then S is regular.

source.place: Lemma 031E (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/031E), at each target prime; the final ascent in the proof of More on Algebra, Lemma 07QI.

proof.text: Fix q in Spec S and let p=q∩R. The local map R_p → S_q is flat and local. Its source is regular local and its target Noetherian.

Use the prime–fibre correspondence to obtain a prime Q in p.Fiber S contracting to q. The localization at Q is isomorphic to S_q/(pR_p)S_q; identify the extended maximal ideal by mapping p through the local homomorphism. The regularity hypothesis on p.Fiber S makes this closed fibre regular local. This is exactly Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂, with transport of the equality of contracted primes.
Apply the flat local regularity criterion 031E. Every S_q is regular local, so isRegularRing_iff proves regularity of S. If S is zero there are no primes and this last condition is vacuous.
